paper.title: Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I
paper.result: Section 6.3 and table 3 discuss a different thirteen-part November 3 Mackensen report. The bounded search for ultimatum and p175 C / p176 A body references located no separate discussion of these three parts. Shared Rustschuk/Hermannstadt geography does not prove an identical plaintext.

comments.result: Norbert and Max Baertl discuss existing p176a, corresponding to source part 4. That credit is retained; new companions do not independently validate its supplied missing symbols.

limits: C1 retains JUDORT,1XAX11212OM and24X24 exactly. No historical reference-number or hour assignment is inferred.
C2 repeats the same unknown square cell GF twice: the two time digits must agree under an unchanged key, but their value remains 56789.
A5 retains VERPFLEG?Z and its conjunction UND; no completion or repair of the odd ending is asserted.
C3 and A6 are preserved outside readable-record and summary counts. The advertised lengths do not supply missing plaintext.
The earlier p176a breakthrough proposal is separately attributed and excluded from all new-record totals.

rejected_header_transcription.status: The enlarged source shows RICHI-222. The fifteen-coordinate loss arose from a rejected header transcription and is not a historical source model or a candidate frame.
